# tom

53. Taxi driver, Sheffield. BMI 36 at the record's start. Knee ache from
decades in and out of the cab, a blood-pressure tablet since 2027, two full
loss-regain cycles behind him before the one that finally holds. Wife Lin,
daughter Kelly, grandson Jack. Synthetic; any resemblance to a real person is
accidental and unintended.

## In his own words

"I've done the crash thing. Got down to fourteen stone in nine months once,
felt like a new man, and then the job put it straight back on me plus a bit
more, because sitting in a cab twelve hours a day doesn't care how good your
January was.

I don't do apps. Never have, never will. I've a notebook by the bathroom
scale and I fill it in when I remember, and every few months our Kelly makes
me type it all into her spreadsheet because she says otherwise it's just a
book nobody reads. I'm not going to pretend that's the same as weighing every
day. It isn't.

The stairs are what I actually watch. Fourteen of them, I put the bannister
in myself twenty year back. Twelve of fourteen without stopping, most days
now. That's mine, that doesn't go in anybody's spreadsheet."

## The record his life produces

- Five years, 2025-07-01 to 2030-06-30. Sparse throughout - a notebook, not a
  habit tracker.
- Weight: 325 ordinary weigh-ins plus the regain-peak row and the row that
  corrects it, transcribed from the notebook into the file in nine batches,
  each batch landing months after the dates it covers.
- Measurements: 27 waist-tape readings, the one number he actually trusts,
  logged the evening he takes them rather than batched.
- Sessions: 118 rows, all manual, all athlete-stated - a Sunday reservoir
  walk when the knee allows it, a Thursday swim at the leisure centre. No
  device has ever touched this record.
- Daily: six rows in five years, notes on days that mattered, never a step
  count or a sleep hour - there is no wearable in this life.
- Medical: a standing knee restriction from before the record starts, four
  short flares on top of it, and a blood-pressure medication row.
- Goals: three eras - a crash goal he achieved, a recovery goal he later
  abandoned, and a modest guarded goal still running at the record's end.
- Journal: one row, a claimed six-week streak with nothing in the record
  that could confirm or deny it.

## The axis he stresses

A five-year record with a real middle: not a straight line in either
direction, but a crash, a full regain, a second attempt that gives up on its
own deadline, and only then a slow, honest, guarded descent. Layered on top:
a transcription habit that quietly rounds him lighter than he is, and one
single correction that goes the other way - flattering, timed exactly at the
regain's peak, and preserved forever underneath the row that replaces it.
